title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this second draft of 'Analysis situs' (June 1986), Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic 'atlas' structure. The data are a set M of elementary pieces ('multiplicités': points, lines, cells), relations ≤ (face or inclusion), ≪ (lies in), ∘≪ (lies in the interior), the non-incidence relation ≭, and parallelism ∥ on lines. A figure F has an underlying set F̃ ⊂ M, closed under the relevant faces. G ≤ F means G is a sub-figure (G̃ ⊂ F̃). F' ≪ F means F' lies in F; the next page shows each cell X' of F' lies in the interior of a unique cell X of F, which reads like 'F' is a subdivision of part of F'.

Top of page (axiom bookkeeping): At 9 follows from the two variants At 9' and At 9'' introduced on the previous page. The top-right margin note (*) appears to state a candidate axiom At 10 for lines: for X, Y ∈ M with X ≠ Y and X ≭ Y, conclude X ∥ Y. This is the analogue of (1.59) on the previous page, with the remark that it is not an a priori axiom and a forward reference to p. 72. The diagonal margins sort At 8, At 9, At 10 (and At 11 'plus bas') into 'axiomes d'existence' versus 'axiomes de liaison'. This is Hilbert-style vocabulary (Verknüpfung = incidence axioms) for organising the system. 'Le cas essentiel' appears to be Y ⊂ X.

Main content, dated '21 juin': assume atlas axioms At 1 – At 7.

Proposition. Let F ∈ 𝓕, F' ≪ F, and G ≤ F. Then G' = Inf^≪(F', G), the greatest figure lying in both F' and G for ≪, exists. Moreover G' is a sub-figure of F', given by
(1.60) G̃' = {X ∈ F̃' | X ≪ G},
with a commutative square G' ≤ F', G ≤ F, G' ≪ G.

In modern terms: if F' is a subdivision of (part of) a cell complex F and G is a subcomplex of F, then the cells of F' lying in |G| form a subcomplex G' of F'. That subcomplex is the restriction of the subdivision to G, and it is the meet of F' and G.

Demonstration (begun here, finished on p. 65). Formula (1.60) defines a subset of F̃'. It is closed under faces by transitivity, since ≤ implies ≪, so it defines a sub-figure G' of F', and clearly G' ≪ G. On p. 65 the universal property is proved. By At 4 one reduces to Φ = Z ∈ M. Take the smallest X' ∈ F̃' with Z ≪ X', and the unique X ∈ F̃ with X' ∘≪ X. At 7 gives Z ∘≪ X, so X is the smallest element of F̃^Z. Since Z ≪ G there is Y ∈ G̃ ⊂ F̃ with Z ≪ Y, hence X ≤ Y and X' ≪ X ≤ Y ≤ G. The argument shows that existence of this particular Inf can be proved rather than postulated ('Mais sans admettre l'existence des Inf').

Purpose: to build a purely combinatorial or set-theoretic 'tame' calculus of figures and their subdivisions. This is consistent with the géométrie modérée / analysis situs program sketched in the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The final line is cut off: 'on a évidemment G' ≪ F par …'. Presumably what is intended is G' ≪ G (or G' ≤ F'), justified on the next page.

The proof relies on At 4 (reduction to elements of M) and At 7 (transitivity of ∘≪ through refinement), as the next page shows. The existence of minimal elements of F̃'^Z is implicitly an axiom of the atlas.

ideas.what: Restriction of a refinement F' ≪ F to a sub-figure G ≤ F: G' = {X ∈ F̃' : X ≪ G} is a sub-figure of F' and equals the meet Inf^≪(F', G)
ideas.modern_name: restriction of a subdivision to a subcomplex; meets in the poset of subcomplexes/subdivisions (PL topology, regular CW / polyhedral complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard PL topology folklore (Alexander, Newman, Whitehead; Rourke–Sanderson textbook treatment)

ideas.what: Classifying the atlas axioms into 'axiomes d'existence' and 'axiomes de liaison', Hilbert-style, and deriving At 9 from At 9' and At 9''
ideas.modern_name: incidence-geometry style axiomatization of a combinatorial (tame) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hilbert, Grundlagen der Geometrie (axiom groups); tame/o-minimal frameworks by van den Dries et al.
ideas.where_published: Only the general program of 'topologie modérée' appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6

ideas.what: Candidate axiom for lines: distinct non-incident lines are parallel (X ≠ Y, X ≭ Y ⇒ X ∥ Y), flagged as not an a priori axiom
ideas.modern_name: parallelism defined via disjointness in affine incidence geometry

missed.claim: The page carries a date '21. juin' (1986), outside the catalogue's stated range 18–20/06/1986 for cote 156-6. This is a small metadata correction for the archive record.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Accurate dating of the Analysis situs drafts matters for reconstructing the chronology of Grothendieck's 1986 work on tame topology alongside Récoltes et Semailles.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'Atlas' approach to analysis situs is an unpublished attempt at a set-theoretic/combinatorial foundation for tame topology. It has axioms At 1–At 11, figures, refinements ≪ and interiors ∘≪, and has not been systematically reconstructed or compared with o-minimality or with the face-poset theory of regular CW complexes. This page's own content is routine.
missed.quote: Les axiomes At 8, At 9, At 10 … axiomes de liaison
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A comparison with o-minimal structures and combinatorial models of stratified spaces could show whether his axiom system is a genuinely distinct foundation. Its value for that comparison is modest and uncertain.

deep.surprise_reason: The proposition is a standard fact about restricting subdivisions to subcomplexes, proved inside a private axiom system. The only points of interest are the organisation of the axioms (existence vs. liaison) and the archival date discrepancy.
transcription_corrections: The page header reads 'At 9 est impliqué par deux axiomes At 9', At 9''' (the previous page writes 'Af'; it is the same At = Atlas axiom family).
The top-right margin likely reads: 'At 10: X, Y ∈ M, X ≠ Y, (i.e. lignes) X ≭ Y ⇒ X ∥ Y', followed by a remark that this is not an a priori axiom, with a reference to 'p. 72' (marked (*)).
'Soient 𝓕 une [?] … At 1 – [-At 6-] At 7' is probably 'Soient 𝓕 un atlas satisfaisant At 1 – At 7' (At 6 is crossed out and replaced by At 7).
A date '21. juin' is written in the left margin above 'Proposition'.

'Il en [?] faut que … l'existence des Inf, Mais sans admettre' probably reads 'Il en faut admettre l'existence des Inf. Mais sans admettre …', i.e. the existence is to be proved here rather than postulated.
The last line is probably 'et on a évidemment G' ≪ G (or G' ≤ F') par …'.
